testo_originale: 1. testo_originale: Article 6 Recording and registering of restrictions

testo_originale: 2. testo_originale: 3. The record and, where applicable, the documents containing underlying factual and legal elements shall be registered. They shall be made available to the European Data Protection Supervisor on request.

testo_originale: Article 7 Duration of restrictions
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a relatively narrow scope: it regulates the temporal application of a restriction by fixing how long it lasts. testo_originale: 1. The restrictions referred to in Articles 3, 4 and 5 shall continue to apply as long as the reasons justifying them remain applicable.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational continuation clause that governs the duration of previously imposed restrictions. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not create the restriction itself or set a general principle, but only specifies when the existing measure must keep applying.

testo_originale: 2. Where the reasons for a restriction referred to in Article 3 or 5 no longer apply, the Commission shall lift the restriction and provide the principal reasons for the restriction to the data subject. At the same time, the Commission shall inform the data subject of the possibility of lodging a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor at any time or of seeking a judicial remedy in the Court of Justice of the European Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow procedural trigger: it applies only when an earlier restriction ceases to be justified and then prescribes the immediate follow-up steps. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle, but instead fixes a specific sequence of actions and notifications in a defined situation.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall review the application of the restrictions referred to in Articles 3 and 5 one year after adoption and at the closure of the relevant Commission analyses and procedures carried out with regard to the screening of foreign direct investments or the cooperation mechanism under Regulation (EU) 2019/452. Thereafter, the Commission shall monitor the need to maintain any restriction. The review shall include an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the restriction, taking into account the relevant elements set out in Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a procedural review obligation, sitting toward the specific end of the spectrum. It does not establish the framework’s general principles, but instead prescribes when and how an existing restriction must be reassessed, including the criteria to be applied and the ongoing monitoring duty.

testo_originale: Article 8 Review by the Data Protection Officer of the Commission 1. The Data Protection Officer of the Commission shall be informed, without undue delay, whenever data subjects’ rights are restricted in accordance with this Decision. Upon request, the Data Protection Officer shall be provided with access to the record and any documents containing underlying factual and legal elements. 2. The Data Protection Officer may request a review of the restriction. The Data Protection Officer shall be informed about the outcome of the requested review. 3. The Commission shall document the involvement of the Data Protection Officer in each case where the application of rights and obligations referred to in Article 2(2) is restricted.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision establishing an internal review and documentation mechanism within the framework. It does not set a general principle or define the regime, but specifies who must be notified, what access may be granted, and how the review process is to be recorded in individual cases.

descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it sits below the basic enabling framework and above purely technical implementation, because it identifies the specific procedural areas covered by the act and signals that more detailed rules follow. testo_originale: (c) and Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560; (4) detailed rules on disclosure, access to file and confidential information pursuant to Article 42 and Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560; (5) the form, content and procedural details of transparency requirements; (6) detailed rules on the calculation of time limits; (7) the procedural details and time limits for proposing commitments under Article 25 and 31 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560.

testo_originale: Article 2 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply: (1) ‘Notifying parties’ for the purpose of notifications of concentrations means persons or undertakings required to submit a notification pursuant to Article 21(3) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560. (2) ‘Other persons involved’ for the purpose of notifications of concentrations mean persons involved in the proposed concentration other than the notifying parties, such as the seller and the undertaking or part of the undertaking that is the target of the concentration. (3) ‘Notifying parties’ for the purpose of notifications and declarations regarding foreign financial contributions in public procurement’ means all economic operators, groups of economic operators, main subcontractors and main suppliers covered by the notification obligation in accordance with Article 29(5) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560. (4) ‘Working days’ means all days other than Saturdays, Sundays, and Commission holidays as published in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational, bordering on technical: this is a definitions clause that fixes the meaning of key terms for use throughout the instrument. It does not lay down a general principle or allocate powers; instead, it supplies interpretive building blocks that support the application of more specific procedural rules.

testo_originale: Article 3 Persons entitled to submit notifications and declarations
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision that identifies the category of actors allowed to trigger the procedural mechanism, placing it above purely operational detail but below foundational principles. testo_originale: 1. Notifications of concentrations pursuant to Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 shall be submitted by the notifying parties as referred in Article 2, point (1). Each notifying party shall be responsible for the correctness of the information provided by it.

testo_originale: 2. Notifications and declarations in public procurement procedures shall be submitted to the contracting authority or contracting entity by the economic operator, or, in the case of groups of economic operators, main subcontractors and main suppliers, the main contractor or main concessionaire, referred to in Article 29(6) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 on its behalf and on behalf of any and all notifying parties as referred to in Article 2, point (3). descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that specifies who must file the required submissions and how responsibility for the information is allocated among the parties. testo_originale: 3. Where notifications or declarations are signed by authorised external representatives of persons or of undertakings, such representatives shall produce written proof that they are authorised to act.

testo_originale: Article 4 Prior notification of concentrations

testo_originale: 1. Notifications of concentrations pursuant to Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 shall be submitted using the form for notifying concentrations set out in Annex I. Joint notifications pursuant to Article 21(3) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 shall be submitted on a single form.

testo_originale: 2. The form for notifying concentrations and all relevant supporting documents shall be submitted to the Commission in accordance with Article

testo_originale: 3. Notifications shall be submitted in one of the official languages of the Union. testo_originale: 4. The Commission may, upon written request, dispense a requesting notifying party with the obligation to provide any information in the notification form set out in Annex I, including documents, or with any other requirement in the notification form related to this information.

testo_originale: 5. The Commission shall without delay acknowledge in writing to the notifying parties receipt of the notification and of any reply to a letter sent by the Commission pursuant to Article 6(2) and (3).

testo_originale: Article 5 Notifications and declarations of foreign financial contributions in the context of public procurement procedures

testo_originale: 1. Notifications of foreign financial contributions in the context of public procurement procedures shall be submitted using the form set out in Annex II on one form containing information regarding all of the notifying parties related to one tender or request to participate, to the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the relevant public procurement procedure in line with Article 29(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that specifies the concrete filing method for a particular procedural step, rather than laying down a general principle. testo_originale: 2. Where, in public procurement procedures meeting the thresholds in Articles 28(1)(a) and 28(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, no notifiable foreign financial contributions in the last 3 years have been granted by a third country to the notifying parties, those parties must submit, instead of a notification, a declaration. In accordance with Articles 4(3) and 29(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, foreign financial contributions the total amount of which per third country is lower than the amount of de minimis aid as defined in Article 3(2), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EU) No 1407/2013 over the consecutive period of three years preceding the declaration do not have to be reported in the declaration.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational, with a technical sub-rule character: it sets a specific filing alternative and a precise reporting exemption triggered by defined conditions. Its abstraction level is low because it does not establish a general principle or institutional structure, but instead prescribes the exact procedural form and threshold-based detail for one narrowly defined situation.

testo_originale: 3. The notification, including all relevant supporting documents, or the declaration shall be transferred by the contracting authority or contracting entity to the Commission in accordance with Article
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision specifying a concrete transmission step within an already established procedure — it sits below the structural level because it does not create the framework, but tells a particular actor how a required filing is to be passed on. testo_originale: 5. The Commission may, upon written request by the notifying parties, and informing the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the public procurement procedure, dispense a requesting notifying party with the obligation to provide any information in the notification form set out in Annex II, including documents, or with any other requirement in the notification form related to that information.

testo_originale: 6. The Commission shall without delay acknowledge the receipt of the notification or declaration and of any reply to a letter sent by the Commission pursuant to Article 7(1) and (3), in writing to the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the public procurement procedure, with a copy of the acknowledgment sent to the notifying parties or their authorised external representatives.

testo_originale: Article 6 Effective date of notification in concentrations
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision at a fairly specific level: it does not set a general principle, but fixes the point in time from which a procedural step is treated as effective. Its function is to supply a concrete rule for a defined procedural situation, making it more technical than structural and clearly subordinate to the broader framework.

testo_originale: 1. Pursuant to Article 24(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, the effective date of a notification shall be the date on which the Commission receives a complete notification.
descrizione_funzionale: Technical operational rule fixing the legal trigger point for a procedural step within a pre-existing framework. It sits near the most specific end of the spectrum because it does not establish a general principle or allocate powers, but instead sets a precise rule for when a particular filing is treated as effective.

testo_originale: 2. Where the Commission finds that the information, including documents, contained in the notification is incomplete, the Commission shall inform the notifying parties or their authorised external representatives in writing without delay. In such cases, the notification shall become effective on the date on which the complete information is received by the Commission.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a technical procedural trigger: it specifies what happens when a filing is incomplete and ties legal effectiveness to receipt of the missing information. It sits near the lower end of the hierarchy because it does not set a general principle or allocate powers, but instead fixes a concrete step and consequence within a defined process.

testo_originale: 3. After notification, the notifying parties shall communicate to the Commission without delay any relevant information, including material changes in the facts, which the notifying parties would have had to notify if they had known or ought to have known that information at the time of notification. Where that information could have a significant effect on the Commission’s assessment of the notified concentration, the Commission may consider the notification to become effective only on the date on which it receives the information concerned. The Commission shall inform the notifying parties or their representatives of this in writing without delay.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow procedural function: it regulates what must happen after an initial filing and how the authority may react if later information is missing or changes. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it specifies a concrete post-notification duty, a conditional consequence, and a communication requirement rather than laying down a general principle or institutional power.

testo_originale: 4. For the purposes of this Article, the provision of incorrect or misleading information shall be considered as rendering the notification incomplete.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational definition within a procedural rule, sitting toward the technical end of the hierarchy. It does not set a general principle or allocate powers; instead, it clarifies a specific legal consequence for one identified procedural condition, thereby refining how completeness is assessed in a concrete case.

testo_originale: Article 7 Effective date of notifications and declarations of foreign financial contributions in the context of public procurement procedures
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision at a relatively specific level: it governs when a filing is treated as effective within a defined procedural context. Its placement is technical because it fixes the operative trigger for a particular step in the process, rather than laying down a general principle or institutional framework.

testo_originale: 1. In open public procurement procedures within the meaning of Article 27 of Directive 2014/24/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ) , notifications and declarations shall become effective on the date on which they are received by the Commission. In multi-stage public procurement procedures, a notification or declaration submitted at the stage of the submission of the request to participate as well as the updated notification or updated declaration submitted at the stage of the submission of the final tender according to Article 29(1), last sentence, of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, shall become effective on the date on which they are received by the Commission. However, where the Commission finds that the information, including documents, contained in the received notification or declaration is incomplete, the Commission shall inform the notifying parties or their authorised external representatives in writing without delay. In such cases, the notification or declaration shall become effective on the date on which the complete information pursuant to Article 29(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 is received by the Commission.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule with a technical focus: it fixes when filings take legal effect and how incompleteness affects that timing. Its abstraction level is low because it does not set a general principle or allocate powers, but instead specifies a concrete procedural trigger and a corrective mechanism for a defined filing scenario.

testo_originale: 2. Where the relevant contracting authority or contracting entity exercises its rights pursuant to Article 56(3) of Directive 2014/24/EU or Article 76(4) of Directive 2014/25/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ) , to ask for clarifications of the notification, declaration, updated notification or updated declaration according to Article 29(1), last sentence, and Article 29(3) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, and decides to reject the tender or request to participate for lack of clarifications where not duly provided, the notification or declaration shall be considered not to have been made nor transferred to the Commission.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational and technical: it sets a conditional consequence for a very specific procedural situation, triggered only if a particular clarification request is made and not properly answered. Its function is to fix the legal effect of that narrow scenario, rather than to state a general principle or organise the framework at a higher level.

testo_originale: 3. After the submission of a notification, declaration, updated notification or updated declaration, the notifying parties shall communicate to the Commission without delay any relevant new information, including changes in the facts, which the notifying parties would have had to notify if they had known or ought to have known that information at the time of the submission of the complete notification or declaration or updated notification or updated declaration. Where that information could have a significant effect on the Commission’s assessment, the Commission may consider the notification, declaration, updated notification or updated declaration to become effective only on the date on which it receives the relevant information. The Commission shall inform the notifying parties of notifications in the context of public procurement procedures or their external representatives, as well as the relevant contracting authority or contracting entity of the date of effectiveness in writing and without delay.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a strong technical character: it lays down a post-filing information duty and the procedural consequence of late-received material information. It sits at the most specific end of the hierarchy because it does not lay down a general principle or procedure, but simply updates the legal content by replacing one listed component with another.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Terminal commencement clause fixing the point at which the act becomes legally effective — it sits at the most technical end of the hierarchy because it does not create substantive rules, only determines when the instrument starts to apply. Its function is purely operational, setting a formal effective date within the legal framework.

testo_originale: Article 1 Subject matter and scope
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational provision at the top of the hierarchy, because it defines the instrument’s subject matter and the outer limits of its application. It is structural rather than operational: it frames what the act covers without laying down any concrete procedure, threshold, or enforcement detail.

testo_originale: 1. This Regulation establishes a framework for the screening by Member States of foreign direct investments into the Union on the grounds of security or public order and for a mechanism for cooperation between Member States, and between Member States and the Commission, with regard to foreign direct investments likely to affect security or public order. It includes the possibility for the Commission to issue opinions on such investments.
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational provision that sets out the Regulation’s overall scope and institutional architecture, so it sits at the highest level of abstraction. It establishes the framework, identifies the main actors and cooperation mechanism, and signals an ancillary Commission role, without laying down any concrete procedure or technical criterion.

testo_originale: 2. This Regulation is without prejudice to each Member State having sole responsibility for its national security, as provided for in Article 4(2) TEU, and to the right of each Member State to protect its essential security interests in accordance with Article 346 TFEU.
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational safeguard clause that preserves pre-existing constitutional competences and core state prerogatives, sitting near the top of the hierarchy as a limiting principle for the whole instrument. It does not set an operative procedure or technical condition; instead, it frames the regulation’s reach by carving out a general reservation of authority.

testo_originale: 3. Nothing in this Regulation shall limit the right of each Member State to decide whether or not to screen a particular foreign direct investment within the framework of this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural safeguard clause preserving national discretion within the framework, so it sits at an intermediate level rather than a foundational one. It does not create a general principle or a detailed procedure; instead, it delineates the scope of the framework by reserving a core decision-making choice to the Member States.

testo_originale: Article 2 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply: (1) ‘foreign direct investment’ means an investment of any kind by a foreign investor aiming to establish or to maintain lasting and direct links between the foreign investor and the entrepreneur to whom or the undertaking to which the capital is made available in order to carry on an economic activity in a Member State, including investments which enable effective participation in the management or control of a company carrying out an economic activity; (2) ‘foreign investor’ means a natural person of a third country or an undertaking of a third country, intending to make or having made a foreign direct investment; (3) ‘screening’ means a procedure allowing to assess, investigate, authorise, condition, prohibit or unwind foreign direct investments; (4) ‘screening mechanism’ means an instrument of general application, such as a law or regulation, and accompanying administrative requirements, implementing rules or guidelines, setting out the terms, conditions and procedures to assess, investigate, authorise, condition, prohibit or unwind foreign direct investments on grounds of security or public order; (5) ‘foreign direct investment undergoing screening’ means a foreign direct investment undergoing a formal assessment or investigation pursuant to a screening mechanism; (6) ‘screening decision’ means a measure adopted in application of a screening mechanism; (7) ‘undertaking of a third country’ means an undertaking constituted or otherwise organised under the laws of a third country.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly structural and near-foundational: this is a definitions clause that fixes the legal meaning of core terms used throughout the instrument. It does not itself regulate conduct or set procedures; instead, it supplies the conceptual architecture that conditions how the rest of the framework operates.

testo_originale: Article 3 Screening mechanisms of Member States
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision at an intermediate level: it sets out the existence and basic architecture of a national screening mechanism, rather than laying down a detailed operational test. Its function is to organise the framework by establishing the core institutional arrangement and the conditions under which such a mechanism may operate.

testo_originale: 1. In accordance with this Regulation, Member States may maintain, amend or adopt mechanisms to screen foreign direct investments in their territory on the grounds of security or public order.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural empowerment clause: it authorises Member States to maintain, amend, or introduce screening mechanisms within the framework, so it sits above operational detail but below a foundational statement of purpose. Its abstraction level is intermediate because it allocates regulatory competence and sets the permissible grounds for action without prescribing the concrete procedure or criteria to be used.

testo_originale: 2. Rules and procedures related to screening mechanisms, including relevant timeframes, shall be transparent and not discriminate between third countries. In particular, Member States shall set out the circumstances triggering the screening, the grounds for screening and the applicable detailed procedural rules.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision that sets governing requirements for how screening mechanisms must be designed and applied, rather than laying down a broad principle alone. It sits below foundational provisions because it translates the framework into concrete procedural standards and mandatory content elements, including triggers, grounds, and time limits.

testo_originale: 3. Member States shall apply timeframes under their screening mechanisms. The screening mechanisms shall allow Member States to take into account the comments of other Member States referred to in Article 6 and 7 and the opinions of the Commission referred to in Articles 6, 7 and
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule setting a procedural requirement for how national screening mechanisms must be run, rather than a broad principle or institutional allocation. It is specific because it fixes a timing-related obligation and requires the mechanism to accommodate external comments and opinions within the process, making it a concrete implementation detail within the framework.

testo_originale: 4. Confidential information, including commercially-sensitive information, made available to the Member State undertaking the screening shall be protected.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational safeguard clause that imposes a concrete protection duty within the screening process, rather than setting out a general principle for the whole framework. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it specifies a particular handling rule for a defined category of information in a specific procedural context.

testo_originale: 5. Foreign investors and the undertakings concerned shall have the possibility to seek recourse against screening decisions of the national authorities.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational safeguard clause: it sets a concrete procedural entitlement within the framework, rather than laying down a general principle or institutional structure. Its abstraction level is relatively low because it specifies a particular legal remedy available against a defined category of decisions, without further elaborating the broader system.

testo_originale: 6. Member States which have a screening mechanism in place shall maintain, amend or adopt measures necessary to identify and prevent circumvention of the screening mechanisms and screening decisions.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision imposing a concrete implementation duty on Member States already operating a screening mechanism. It sits near the specific end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or institutional structure, but instead requires targeted measures to identify and prevent circumvention in the application of existing mechanisms and decisions.

testo_originale: 7. Member States shall notify the Commission of their existing screening mechanisms by 10 May
descrizione_funzionale: Technical-operational clause, near the bottom of the hierarchy. It fixes a concrete notification obligation and a specific deadline, so it implements the framework through a precise procedural requirement rather than laying down a general principle or structural rule.

testo_originale: 2019. Member States shall notify the Commission of any newly adopted screening mechanism or any amendment to an existing screening mechanism within 30 days of the entry into force of the newly adopted screening mechanism or of any amendment to an existing screening mechanism.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision imposing a concrete notification duty on Member States, with a fixed 30-day deadline. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or allocate broad powers, but instead prescribes a specific procedural step triggered by a defined event.

testo_originale: 8. No later than three months after having received the notifications referred to in paragraph 7, the Commission shall make publicly available a list of Member States' screening mechanisms. The Commission shall keep that list up to date.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision setting a concrete administrative duty and a time-bound publication requirement, with an ongoing maintenance obligation. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish the framework’s principles or structure, but instead specifies how one procedural output must be handled in practice.

It sits above purely operational rules because it does not itself impose a concrete outcome, but it organises the evaluative parameters to be used in subsequent application.

testo_originale: 1. testo_originale: 2. For each reporting period, Member States that maintain screening mechanisms shall, in addition to the information referred to in paragraph 1, provide aggregated information on the application of their screening mechanisms.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that specifies a recurring reporting obligation for a defined subset of addressees, rather than laying down a general principle. testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall provide an annual report on the implementation of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council. That report shall be made public.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a reporting obligation and publication requirement, sitting near the practical end of the hierarchy. It does not set the framework’s core principles or define competences; instead, it specifies a recurring accountability mechanism and a concrete transparency step.

testo_originale: 4. The European Parliament may invite the Commission to a meeting of its committee responsible to present and explain systemic issues related to the implementation of this Regulation.

testo_originale: Article 6 Cooperation mechanism in relation to foreign direct investments undergoing screening
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision that organises how authorities interact within the framework, so it sits above purely operational rules but below the broadest foundational statements. testo_originale: 1. Member States shall notify the Commission and the other Member States of any foreign direct investment in their territory that is undergoing screening by providing the information referred to in Article 9(2) of this Regulation as soon as possible. The notification may include a list of Member States whose security or public order is deemed likely to be affected. As part of the notification, and where applicable, the Member State undertaking the screening shall endeavour to indicate whether it considers that the foreign direct investment undergoing screening is likely to fall within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision setting out a concrete notification obligation within an already established procedure. It sits low on the abstraction spectrum because it specifies who must act, what information must be provided, and when the communication should occur, rather than laying down a general principle or delegating rule-making power.

testo_originale: 2. Where a Member State considers that a foreign direct investment undergoing screening in another Member State is likely to affect its security or public order, or has information relevant for such screening, it may provide comments to the Member State undertaking the screening. The Member State providing comments shall send those comments to the Commission simultaneously. The Commission shall notify the other Member States that comments were provided.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision setting out a concrete intergovernmental notification and comment mechanism triggered by a specific condition. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish the framework’s general principles, but instead prescribes a particular procedural step and communication duty within an already defined process.

testo_originale: 3. Where the Commission considers that a foreign direct investment undergoing screening is likely to affect security or public order in more than one Member State, or has relevant information in relation to that foreign direct investment, it may issue an opinion addressed to the Member State undertaking the screening. The Commission may issue an opinion irrespective of whether other Member States have provided comments. The Commission may issue an opinion following comments from other Member States. The Commission shall issue such opinion where justified, after at least one third of Member States consider that a foreign direct investment is likely to affect their security or public order. The Commission shall notify the other Member States that an opinion was issued.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that sets out when a specific institutional intervention may or must occur, and the conditions triggering it. It sits below structural rules because it does not define the framework’s general principles or competences, but instead specifies a concrete decision-making procedure and threshold for action in a particular case.

testo_originale: 4. A Member State which duly considers that a foreign direct investment in its territory is likely to affect its security or public order may request the Commission to issue an opinion or other Member States to provide comments.

It sits below the structural level because it does not set a general principle or allocate broad competences, but instead specifies when a particular procedural step may be triggered and by whom.

testo_originale: 5. The comments referred to in paragraph 2 and the opinions referred to in paragraph 3 shall be duly justified.

The list of projects or programmes of Union interest is set out in the Annex.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational definition clause that narrows a general category by specifying the criteria for inclusion and pointing to an annexed list. It sits toward the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a broad principle or allocate powers, but instead fixes a concrete interpretive threshold for applying the provision.

testo_originale: 4. The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 16 to amend the list of projects and programmes of Union interest.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural empowerment clause: it authorises the Commission to update a predefined list through delegated legislation, so it sits above purely operational detail but below foundational principles. Its abstraction level is intermediate because it allocates rule-making competence and sets the mechanism for amendment, without itself laying down the substantive content of the list.

testo_originale: Article 9 Information requirements
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it sits below the framework’s general principles but above purely technical implementation, because it sets out an information-gathering obligation that supports the functioning of the regime. Its abstraction level is moderate, since it does not define the overall policy or institutional architecture, but instead specifies a concrete procedural requirement to be followed in a particular context.

testo_originale: 1. Member States shall ensure that the information notified pursuant to Article 6(1) or requested by the Commission and other Member States pursuant to Articles 6(6) and 7(5) is made available to the Commission and the requesting Member States without undue delay.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision imposing a concrete information-sharing obligation within an already established procedure. It sits below the structural rules because it does not create the framework or define competences, but instead specifies how an existing duty must be carried out in practice and with what timing.

testo_originale: 2. The information referred to in paragraph 1 shall include:
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that opens a disclosure list by specifying the minimum content to be provided under a prior rule. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not create the duty itself or set the broader standard, but merely structures its concrete implementation by introducing the items that must follow.

testo_originale: (a) the ownership structure of the foreign investor and of the undertaking in which the foreign direct investment is planned or has been completed, including information on the ultimate investor and participation in the capital;
descrizione_funzionale: Operational, with a fairly technical level of abstraction: it specifies one concrete item of information to be examined within a broader assessment. Its function is to fix a particular evidentiary criterion, not to state a general principle or allocate institutional powers.

testo_originale: (b) the approximate value of the foreign direct investment;
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational and technical: it fixes one concrete item of information to be provided within a broader reporting or screening context. Its abstraction level is low because it does not establish a general principle or allocate powers, but instead specifies a precise factual parameter to be assessed.

testo_originale: (c) the products, services and business operations of the foreign investor and of the undertaking in which the foreign direct investment is planned or has been completed;
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational criterion within a broader assessment framework, sitting near the technical end of the spectrum. It does not set a general principle or allocate powers; instead, it identifies one concrete element to be examined in a particular evaluative process.

testo_originale: (d) the Member States in which the foreign investor and the undertaking in which the foreign direct investment is planned or has been completed conduct relevant business operations;
descrizione_funzionale: Technical operative criterion within a broader assessment framework, because it identifies one concrete factual element to be considered in a specific screening context. It does not establish a general principle or institutional arrangement; instead, it supplies a narrow checklist item used to structure the application of an existing rule.

testo_originale: (e) the funding of the investment and its source, on the basis of the best information available to the Member State;
descrizione_funzionale: Technical operative criterion within a broader assessment framework, sitting near the most specific end of the hierarchy. It fixes one concrete evidentiary factor to be considered and qualifies it by reference to the best available information, rather than laying down a general principle or allocating competences.

testo_originale: (f) the date when the foreign direct investment is planned to be completed or has been completed.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational and technical: it fixes a single factual timing element to be identified in a specific notification context. Its function is not to set a general principle or structure, but to supply one concrete data point used in the application of a broader procedure.

testo_originale: 3. Member States shall endeavour to provide any information additional to that referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2, if available, to requesting Member States and to the Commission without undue delay.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision setting a cooperation duty with a qualified standard of timeliness and conditional availability, so it sits near the implementation end of the spectrum. It does not establish the framework itself, but specifies how an existing information-sharing mechanism should be carried out in practice.

testo_originale: 4. The Member State where the foreign direct investment is planned or has been completed may request the foreign investor or the undertaking in which the foreign direct investment is planned or has been completed to provide the information referred to in paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision granting a specific information-request power to a Member State in a defined procedural context. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or framework rule, but instead authorises a concrete step to be taken in a particular case.

testo_originale: 2. The foreign investor or the undertaking concerned shall provide the information requested without undue delay.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision imposing a concrete compliance duty within an information-gathering procedure — it sits near the practical end of the spectrum because it tells a party how to respond once a request has been made. Its specificity comes from fixing the required manner of performance (“without undue delay”) rather than setting a general principle or allocating powers.

testo_originale: 5. A Member State shall notify the Commission and the other Member States concerned without delay, if, in exceptional circumstances, it is unable, despite its best efforts, to obtain the information referred to in paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow procedural trigger: it requires immediate notification only when a specific information-gathering obligation cannot be fulfilled despite best efforts. It sits low on the abstraction scale because it regulates a concrete contingency and prescribes the response, rather than laying down a general principle or structural competence.

testo_originale: 1. In the notification, that Member State shall duly justify the reasons for not providing such information and explain the best efforts undertaken to obtain the information requested, including a request pursuant to paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision within a procedural framework, sitting toward the specific end of the spectrum. It does not set a general principle or define a concept; instead, it prescribes a concrete justification requirement tied to a particular notification step when information cannot be provided.

testo_originale: 4. If no information is provided, any comment issued by another Member State or any opinion issued by the Commission may be based on the information available to them.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision setting a conditional rule for how an assessment may proceed when the preferred input is absent. It sits toward the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish the framework or allocate powers generally, but instead specifies a narrow fallback basis for a particular procedural step.

testo_originale: Article 10 Confidentiality of information transmitted 1. Information received as a result of the application of this Regulation shall be used only for the purpose for which it was requested. 2. Member States and the Commission shall ensure the protection of confidential information acquired in application of this Regulation in accordance with Union and the respective national law. 3. Member States and the Commission shall ensure that classified information provided or exchanged under this Regulation is not downgraded or declassified without the prior written consent of the originator.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational confidentiality rule with a strong technical character: it does not set the framework’s general purpose, but regulates how information handled under the act must be treated. Its specificity comes from prescribing concrete handling constraints and protection requirements, including a particular consent condition for changing classification status.

testo_originale: Article 11 Contact points 1. Each Member State and the Commission shall establish a contact point for the implementation of this Regulation. Member States and the Commission shall involve those contact points on all issues relating to the implementation of this Regulation. 2. A secure and encrypted system shall be provided by the Commission to support direct cooperation and exchange of information between the contact points.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision: it organises the institutional machinery needed to apply the framework by requiring designated contact points and mandating their involvement in implementation. It sits below foundational rules because it does not set substantive criteria or thresholds, but it is more than purely technical since it establishes a standing coordination mechanism and the infrastructure for information exchange.

testo_originale: Article 12 Group of experts on the screening of foreign direct investments into the European Union The group of experts on the screening of foreign direct investments into the European Union providing advice and expertise to the Commission shall continue to discuss issues relating to the screening of foreign direct investments, share best practices and lessons learned, and exchange views on trends and issues of common concern relating to foreign direct investments. The Commission shall also consider seeking the advice of that group on systemic issues relating to the implementation of this Regulation. The discussions in that group shall be kept confidential.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision creating an advisory forum and assigning it ongoing consultative functions within the framework, rather than laying down a general principle. It sits below the foundational level because it organises institutional interaction and working methods, but above the purely technical level because it still frames how the framework is supported and implemented in practice.

testo_originale: Article 13 International Cooperation Member States and the Commission may cooperate with the responsible authorities of third countries on issues relating to the screening of foreign direct investments on grounds of security and public order.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural cooperation clause that authorizes interaction with external authorities within a defined policy area, without laying down any concrete procedure or binding operational test. It sits below foundational provisions because it does not establish the framework’s core principles, but above technical rules because it merely enables coordinated action in general terms.

testo_originale: Article 14 Processing of personal data 1. Any processing of personal data pursuant to this Regulation shall be carried out in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 and only in so far as it is necessary for the screening of foreign direct investments by Member States and for ensuring the effectiveness of the cooperation provided for in this Regulation. 2. Personal data related to the implementation of this Regulation shall be kept only for the time necessary to achieve the purposes for which they were collected.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational safeguard clause that governs how a particular category of information may be handled within the framework, rather than setting the framework’s core architecture. It is specific because it cross-references external rules, imposes a necessity condition, and adds a retention-limit rule, all of which are concrete implementation constraints.

testo_originale: Article 15 Evaluation 1. By 12 October 2023 and every five years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate the functioning and effectiveness of this Regulation and present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council. Member States shall be involved in this exercise and if necessary provide the Commission with additional information for the preparation of that report. 2. Where the report recommends amendments to this Regulation, it may be accompanied by an appropriate legislative proposal.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational, with a strong technical-review character: it does not lay down a general principle or core rule, but instead sets a periodic evaluation mechanism and reporting obligation. Its specificity comes from fixing a timetable, identifying the responsible institution, and providing for a possible follow-up legislative proposal, which makes it a procedural monitoring clause rather than a foundational norm.

testo_originale: Article 16 Exercise of the delegation
descrizione_funzionale: Structural empowerment clause at an intermediate level of abstraction: it governs how a delegated power is to be exercised, rather than laying down a substantive rule itself. Its function is organizational and procedural, because it frames the conditions and limits for secondary rule-making without fixing a concrete operational criterion.

testo_originale: 1. The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural empowerment clause at an intermediate level of abstraction: it allocates delegated rule-making authority to the Commission within a defined legal framework. It does not itself set substantive operational rules, but instead organises how later, more technical norms may be adopted.

testo_originale: 2. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 8(4) shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from 10 April
descrizione_funzionale: Structural empowerment clause conferring delegated rule-making authority on the Commission for an open-ended period — it sits at an intermediate level because it organises institutional competence rather than laying down a substantive rule. Its function is operationally enabling: it authorises future secondary legislation and fixes the temporal scope of that delegation, without itself specifying the detailed content of the rules to be adopted.

testo_originale: 3. The delegation of power referred to in Article 8(4) may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision to revoke shall put an end to the delegation of the power specified in that decision. It shall take effect the day following the publication of the decision in the Official Journal of the European Union or at a later date specified therein. It shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.
descrizione_funzionale: This is a structural delegation-control clause, sitting below foundational provisions but above purely technical implementation details. It does not create a substantive rule; instead, it regulates the legal mechanics of revoking delegated power, including effect, timing, and the non-retroactivity of revocation, which makes it an institutional-operational provision.

testo_originale: 4. Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State in accordance with the principles laid down in the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational consultation requirement within a delegated-rulemaking procedure — it sits below the structural level because it does not create the power itself, but prescribes a mandatory step the Commission must follow before exercising it. Its specificity comes from fixing a concrete procedural condition and identifying the consultation method and participants, rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 5. As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council.
descrizione_funzionale: Technical operational clause governing the post-adoption handling of a delegated act. It sits near the most specific end of the spectrum because it does not create the power itself or set substantive criteria, but merely prescribes a notification step once that power has been exercised.

testo_originale: 6. A delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 8(4) shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed either by the European Parliament or the Council within a period of two months of notification of that act to the European Parliament and the Council or if, before the expiry of that period, the European Parliament and the Council have both informed the Commission that they will not object. That period shall be extended by two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or of the Council.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational, near-technical clause governing the entry into force of a delegated act and the conditions under which it may take effect. It fixes a precise objection period and an extension mechanism, so it does not lay down a general principle but a specific procedural control rule within the delegated-rulemaking process.

testo_originale: Article 17 Entry into force This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . This Regulation shall apply from 11 October 2020.
descrizione_funzionale: Technical commencement clause fixing when the act becomes legally effective and when it starts to apply. It sits at the most operational end of the spectrum because it does not establish any substantive rule or institutional arrangement, but merely sets the temporal trigger for legal effect and application.

testo_originale: Article 1 Regulation (EC) No 601/2006 is amended as follows: (1) Article 2 is replaced by the following: ‘Article 2 Data format Member States shall use SDMX compliant data formats. The Commission (Eurostat) shall make available detailed documentation in relation to these formats and shall supply guidelines on how to implement these formats in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation.’ (2) Article 3 is deleted. (3) The Annex is deleted.
descrizione_funzionale: This is an operational-to-technical amendment clause, because it does not lay down a general principle but rewrites a specific rule on data format and removes existing provisions. Its structural function is to fix a concrete implementation requirement and adjust the supporting annexal framework, which places it near the most detailed end of the hierarchy.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 June 2014.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly technical commencement clause at the operational end of the hierarchy. It fixes the regulation’s entry into force and application date, without creating substantive rules or structuring the framework beyond temporal effect.

testo_originale: Article 1 Subject matter This Regulation establishes a common framework for the systematic production of Community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment.
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational provision that sets the scope and basic architecture of the instrument by establishing the common framework for systematic statistical production. It sits at a high level of abstraction because it frames the regulatory regime as a whole rather than prescribing a concrete procedure, threshold, or technical implementation detail.

testo_originale: Article 2 Submission of data 1. Member States shall submit to the Commission (Eurostat) data on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment as referred to in Annex I. The data shall be as defined in Annex II. 2. Member States shall submit the data to the Commission (Eurostat) in accordance with the deadlines shown in Annex I.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that imposes a concrete reporting obligation and fixes the manner and timing of compliance. It sits below the structural level because it does not define the framework or allocate powers, but instead specifies a practical rule to be carried out according to annexed parameters and deadlines.

testo_originale: Article 3 Data sources 1. Member States shall collect the information required pursuant to this Regulation using all the sources they consider relevant and appropriate. These may include administrative data sources such as business registers. 2. Natural and legal persons required to supply information shall, when responding, comply with the time limits and definitions set by the national institutions responsible for the collection of data within the Member States in accordance with this Regulation. 3. Where the required data cannot be collected at a reasonable cost, best estimates may be transmitted (zero values included).
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that sets out how the information-gathering obligation is to be carried out in practice, rather than laying down a general principle. It specifies permissible sources, compliance parameters, and a fallback method when direct collection is not cost-effective, so it sits close to the technical end of the spectrum.

testo_originale: Article 4 Quality criteria and reports
descrizione_funzionale: Structural to operational provision: it sits below the framework-setting level because it does not state a general principle, but instead organises how compliance is to be assessed and reported. Its abstraction level is intermediate, since it establishes a quality-related requirement and a reporting obligation without descending into the most technical implementation details.

testo_originale: 1. Member States shall take all reasonable measures they consider necessary to ensure the quality of the data transmitted according to common quality standards.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision imposing a general compliance duty on Member States, but only within the data-transmission process and framed by an open-ended reasonableness standard. It sits below foundational or structural rules because it does not create the framework itself; instead, it specifies how an existing obligation must be carried out in practice.

testo_originale: 2. Member States shall supply the Commission with a report on the quality of the data transmitted (hereinafter referred to as ‘quality report’).
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision imposing a concrete reporting obligation on Member States, with a defined output and recipient. It sits below structural rules because it does not set the framework or confer powers, but instead specifies a particular compliance step within the implementation process.

testo_originale: 3. The common quality standards, as well as the content and periodicity of the quality reports, shall be specified in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 11(2), taking into account the implications as regards the cost of collecting and compiling the data as well as important changes concerning data collection. The quality of the data transmitted shall be assessed, on the basis of the quality reports, by the Commission with the assistance of the Balance of Payments Committee referred to in Article
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision that delegates the specification of common standards and reporting content to a later procedure, rather than fixing those details itself. Its abstraction level is intermediate: it sets the rule-making framework and assessment mechanism, but leaves the concrete parameters to be determined through the designated implementing process.

testo_originale: 11. This assessment by the Commission shall be sent to the European Parliament for information.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational notification clause: it does not create a general rule or define a concept, but simply prescribes a follow-up step after a prior assessment has been made. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it allocates a reporting channel and audience for a completed action, without adding substantive criteria or discretion.

testo_originale: 4. Member States shall communicate to the Commission major methodological or other changes that would influence the data transmitted, not later than three months after any such change becomes applicable. The Commission shall notify the European Parliament and the other Member States of any such communication.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational reporting clause that imposes a concrete notification duty tied to a specific triggering event and deadline. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or allocate broad powers, but instead prescribes a precise post-change procedure and communication timeline.

testo_originale: Article 5 Data flows The statistics to be produced shall be grouped for transmission to the Commission (Eurostat) according to the following data flows: (a) balance of payments euro indicators; (b) balance of payments quarterly statistics; (c) international trade in services; (d) foreign direct investment (FDI) flows; (e) FDI positions. The data flows shall be as further specified in Annex I.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that organizes the transmission architecture by dividing outputs into defined reporting streams. It sits below the structural level because it does not set a general principle or confer powers, but instead specifies a concrete classification rule and points to an annex for further technical detail.

testo_originale: Article 6 Reference period and periodicity Member States shall compile the data flows according to the relevant first reference period and the periodicity as specified in Annex I.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that fixes a concrete reporting parameter and points to an annex for the exact timing and frequency. It sits low in the hierarchy because it does not establish a general principle or institutional power, but instead specifies how an existing obligation is to be applied in practice.

testo_originale: Article 7 Transmission of data Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the data required by this Regulation following a format and a procedure defined by the Commission, in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 11(2).
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a technical implementation layer: it imposes a concrete reporting obligation and then leaves the detailed format and procedure to be fixed by the Commission. It sits below structural rules because it does not set the framework itself, but specifies how an already-established obligation must be carried out in practice.

testo_originale: Article 8 Transmission and exchange of confidential data
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision: it sits below the foundational rules and above purely technical details, because it sets out how a specific category of information is to be transmitted and exchanged within the framework. Its abstraction level is moderate-to-low, since it does not define the overall regime but instead specifies an institutional procedure for handling a particular class of data.

testo_originale: 1. Notwithstanding the rules laid down in Article 5(4) of Regulation (Euratom, EEC) No 1588/90, the transmission of confidential data between Eurostat and the ECB may take place to the extent this transmission is necessary to ensure coherence between the balance of payments figures of the European Union and those of the economic territory of the Member States which have adopted the single currency.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational clause with a narrow conditional exception to a pre-existing confidentiality rule, allowing a specific data exchange only where a necessity test is met. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or institutional structure, but instead authorises a particular action in a tightly defined situation.

testo_originale: 2. Paragraph 1 shall apply on condition that the ECB takes due account of the principles defined in Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 322/97 and complies with the conditions laid down in Article 14 of the same Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational cross-reference clause that conditions the application of an earlier rule on compliance with external principles and conditions. It sits below structural provisions because it does not create a general rule or define a concept, but instead adds a specific legal prerequisite for applying one paragraph in practice.

testo_originale: 3. The exchange of confidential data, as defined by Article 13 of Regulation (EC) No 322/97, shall be allowed between Member States where the exchange is necessary to safeguard the quality of the balance of payment figures of the European Union. Member States receiving confidential data from other Member States shall treat that information confidentially.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that authorises a specific form of information exchange under a defined necessity condition and imposes a corresponding confidentiality duty on recipients. It sits below the structural level because it does not set the framework or principles, but instead lays down a concrete rule for a particular situation.

testo_originale: Article 9 Dissemination The Commission (Eurostat) shall disseminate the Community statistics produced pursuant to this Regulation, with a periodicity similar to that specified in Annex I.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that assigns a concrete task to the implementing authority and ties it to a specified reporting rhythm. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or define the framework, but instead prescribes how an existing output is to be published in practice.

testo_originale: Article 10 Adaptation to economic and technical changes The measures necessary to take account of economic and technical changes shall be laid down in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 11(2). Such measures shall concern: (a) the updating of the definitions (Annex II); (b) the updating of data requirements, including submission deadlines as well as revisions, extensions and eliminations of data flows (Annex I).
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational delegation clause: it authorises the adoption of implementing measures to keep the framework aligned with changing conditions, so it sits below the foundational rules but above purely technical application. Its abstraction level is intermediate because it does not itself set the detailed changes; instead, it delegates a bounded power and identifies the categories of matters that may be adjusted.

testo_originale: Article 11 Committee procedure 1. The Commission shall be assisted by a Balance of Payments Committee, hereinafter the ‘Committee’. 2. Where reference is made to this paragraph, Articles 5 and 7 of Decision 1999/468/EC shall apply, having regard to the provisions of Article 8 thereof. The period laid down in Article 5(6) of Decision 1999/468/EC shall be set at three months. 3. The Committee shall adopt its Rules of Procedure. 4. The ECB may attend the meetings of the Committee as an observer.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural and partly operational provision: it organises the institutional machinery for implementing the act by establishing a committee, assigning the applicable decision-making procedure, and allowing internal rules of procedure. Its abstraction level is intermediate because it does not lay down the substantive framework itself, but it does specify how delegated implementation is to be handled in practice, including a concrete time limit.

testo_originale: Article 12 Report on implementation By 28 February 2010, the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and the Council on the implementation of this Regulation. In particular, the report shall: (a) record the quality of the statistics produced; (b) assess the benefits accruing to the Community, the Member States and the providers and users of statistical information of the statistics produced in relation to the costs; (c) identify areas for potential improvement and amendments considered necessary in the light of the results obtained; (d) review the operation of the Committee and recommend whether the scope of implementing measures should be redefined.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational review-and-reporting clause: it sits near the practical end of the hierarchy because it does not set the core framework, but requires a specific post-implementation assessment and follow-up. Its structure is procedural and evaluative, fixing a deadline and listing the matters the report must cover, which makes it a concrete supervisory mechanism rather than a foundational rule.

testo_originale: Article 13 Entry into force This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Terminal commencement clause fixing the point at which the act becomes legally effective — it sits at the most technical end of the hierarchy because it does not establish any substantive rule or institutional arrangement. Its function is purely operational, specifying the timing of applicability rather than a general principle or structural mechanism.

testo_originale: Article 1 Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 is amended as set out in the Annex to this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly technical and operational amendment clause: it does not lay down a general rule or principle, but simply modifies an existing annex by reference to the annex attached to the act. Its function is purely implementative, updating the detailed content of a pre-existing framework without adding any new structural norm.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Terminal commencement clause fixing the date on which the act becomes legally effective — it sits at the most technical end of the hierarchy because it does not establish any substantive rule, only the point from which the amendment starts to apply. Its function is purely operational, determining temporal applicability rather than governing conduct or institutional powers.

testo_originale: Article 1 The notified tax incentive of EUR 401 795 that Portugal is preparing to grant to CORDEX, Companhia Industrial Têxtil S.A., for the purpose of financing its foreign direct investment in Brazil is incompatible with the common market since it does not fulfil the criteria laid down in Article 87(3)(c) of the EC Treaty.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational determination applying a pre-existing compatibility test to a single notified measure — it sits near the specific end of the spectrum because it does not lay down a general rule, but resolves one concrete case by reference to an established legal criterion. Its normative function is case-specific adjudication: it fixes the legal status of one measure by stating that the required conditions are not met.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Decision is addressed to the Portuguese Republic.
descrizione_funzionale: Terminal operational clause identifying the addressee of the decision, with no substantive rule or procedural content. It sits at the technical end of the spectrum because it merely fixes who is bound by the act rather than establishing any general principle, competence, or operative standard.

testo_originale: Article 1 Subject matter and scope 1. Without prejudice to the division of competences established by the TFEU, this Regulation addresses the status of the bilateral investment agreements of the Member States under Union law, and establishes the terms, conditions and procedures under which the Member States are authorised to amend or conclude bilateral investment agreements. 2. For the purpose of this Regulation the term ‘bilateral investment agreement’ means any agreement with a third country that contains provisions on investment protection. This Regulation covers only those provisions of bilateral investment agreements dealing with investment protection.
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational-to-structural provision: it sets the regulatory perimeter and the basic legal architecture of the act, rather than laying down an operational rule. It does so by defining the key term used throughout the instrument and by delimiting the scope and conditions under which the framework applies, which places it above technical implementation but below a pure statement of purpose.

testo_originale: Article 2 Notification to the Commission By 8 February 2013 or within 30 days of the date of their accession to the Union, the Member States shall notify the Commission of all bilateral investment agreements with third countries signed before 1 December 2009 or before the date of their accession, whichever is later, that they either wish to maintain in force or permit to enter into force under this Chapter. The notification shall include a copy of those bilateral investment agreements. Member States shall also notify the Commission of any subsequent changes to the status of those agreements.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that lays down a concrete notification procedure and a fixed deadline for compliance. It sits below the structural level because it does not establish the framework or allocate competences in general terms, but instead specifies a precise administrative step, required content, and timing trigger.

testo_originale: Article 3 Maintenance in force Without prejudice to other obligations of the Member States under Union law, bilateral investment agreements notified pursuant to Article 2 of this Regulation may be maintained in force, or enter into force, in accordance with the TFEU and this Regulation, until a bilateral investment agreement between the Union and the same third country enters into force.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a conditional rule governing a specific transitional situation, rather than a general framework principle. It authorises continued legal effect only under defined circumstances and ties that permission to the occurrence of a later event, making it a concrete implementation clause.

testo_originale: Article 4 Publication 1. Every 12 months the Commission shall publish in the Official Journal of the European Union a list of the bilateral investment agreements notified pursuant to Article 2, Article 11(6) or Article 12(6). 2. The first publication of the list of bilateral investment agreements referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall take place no later than three months after the deadline for notifications made pursuant to Article 2.

descrizione_funzionale: Operational procedural rule: it grants a party under review the right to submit information within a defined assessment step, so it sits toward the concrete end of the spectrum rather than at a foundational level. testo_originale: Article 6 Balancing test 1. descrizione_funzionale: Operational clause that confers a concrete enforcement power and links its exercise to specified legal procedures.
